findings.claim: The PR adds only the tprod form of the bound. Elsewhere in this file each bound of this kind comes as a pair: a HasProd lemma plus the tprod lemma derived from it (HasProd.one_le -> one_le_tprod, HasProd.le_one -> tprod_le_one; additively HasSum.nonneg -> tsum_nonneg). The new proof already proves the HasProd statement inline (`ge_of_tendsto' h.hasProd fun s ↦ s.prod_nonneg ...`) and then discards it. A caller who already has `hf : HasProd f a L` and wants `0 ≤ a` cannot get it from tprod_nonneg. Converting with `HasProd.tprod_eq` needs `[T2Space α]`, and these hypotheses (Preorder + ClosedIciTopology) do not provide it. So that caller has to rebuild the argument by hand from `le_hasProd_of_le_prod` and `Finset.prod_nonneg`.
findings.requested_change:
Add the HasProd version, with the same typeclass assumptions and in the same argument order as HasProd.one_le, and prove tprod_nonneg from it the way one_le_tprod uses HasProd.one_le:

theorem HasProd.nonneg [L.NeBot] {f : ι → α} {a : α} (h : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) (hf : HasProd f a L) : 0 ≤ a :=
  le_hasProd_of_le_prod hf fun s ↦ s.prod_nonneg fun i _ ↦ h i

The multipliable branch of tprod_nonneg then becomes `exact h.hasProd.nonneg hf`. (Consider putting the shared `[CommMonoidWithZero α] [TopologicalSpace α] [Preorder α] [ZeroLEOneClass α] [PosMulMono α] [ClosedIciTopology α]` in a section `variable`.)

findings.claim: `[L.NeBot]` is not needed for a statement about the value of tprod, and the neighbouring tprod lemmas in this file avoid it on purpose. one_le_tprod, tprod_le_one and tprod_le_of_prod_le' handle the `¬L.NeBot` case through `tprod_bot`/finprod, and tsum_nonneg (the additive counterpart, used by the positivity extension for an arbitrary `L`) has no NeBot assumption either. When `¬L.NeBot`, the tprod equals `∏ᶠ i, f i`. That finprod is either a finite product of nonnegative terms or 1, so it is still `≥ 0`. As written, tprod_nonneg is strictly weaker than it needs to be. Any lemma that is generic in `L` and calls it, including a future positivity extension for tprod, would have to carry or synthesize `L.NeBot`.
findings.requested_change:
Drop `[L.NeBot]` from tprod_nonneg (keep it only on HasProd.nonneg) and add the bot case in the same way as one_le_tprod / tprod_le_one:

  by_cases h : Multipliable f L
  · by_cases hL : L.NeBot
    · exact h.hasProd.nonneg hf
    · simp only [tprod_bot hL]
      exact finprod_induction (0 ≤ ·) zero_le_one (fun _ _ ↦ mul_nonneg) hf
  · rw [tprod_eq_one_of_not_multipliable h]
    exact zero_le_one

review_notes: Alternatives inspected: (1) The non-strict neighbour, HasProd.one_le / HasProd.le_one with one_le_tprod / tprod_le_one (and their additive forms HasSum.nonneg / tsum_nonneg). The file pairs a HasProd lemma with a tprod lemma, and the tprod lemmas there drop NeBot through tprod_bot. That decided both findings. (2) The existing general result le_hasProd_of_le_prod. It does let a HasProd caller avoid the new lemma, but it already exists alongside HasProd.one_le and does not make that lemma redundant. The new proof uses exactly this statement, and HasProd.tprod_eq is not available without T2 here, so it does not defeat the analogy. (3) The strict neighbour, Multipliable.one_lt_tprod / Summable.tsum_pos. I did not request a tprod_pos / HasProd.pos analogue. It needs different hypotheses and is false in general: positive factors can multiply to 0, e.g. f n = 1/2 on ℕ in ℝ has HasProd f 0. (4) I did not raise purely stylistic points: ge_of_tendsto' vs le_hasProd_of_le_prod in the proof, simp vs rw in the non-multipliable branch, the binder name x vs i, and the section name/placement.
